narrative: Account expanding — three tickets in six weeks (May–June 2025) covering seat setup, usage-report lag, and a new dashboard for a newly formed analytics team, each resolved within days. No friction, no complaints; this reads as healthy growth rather than risk.
Single ticket, a technical API pagination question resolved in one day. Too sparse to assess relationship health beyond "no problems reported."

Three routine provisioning/admin tickets spread across nearly a year (API access for finance, an alert-digest preference, temporary auditor export access), all resolved within a week. Calm, low-touch account with no sign of friction.
Three tickets over nine months, all straightforward API sandbox and report-template questions, resolved in days. No complaints and no recurring issues — a quiet, healthy account.

Five polite, well-documented tickets from a single named contact (Hanna Lindqvist) over five months covering SSO, export formatting, custom roles, and bulk exports. One ticket — asking why audit log export is "grayed out" despite being a documented Professional-plan feature, filed for a compliance review — was never marked resolved and has no follow-up confirming a fix. The tone stays even throughout, but a dropped compliance-relevant request from a single point of contact is worth checking on directly rather than assuming it resolved itself.

Three tickets over 13 months, all positive in tone ("the new warehouse connector setup was painless", "really pleased with the flexibility") paired with feature requests (template versioning, a Shopify POS connector). Engaged, satisfied account with no friction signals.

A rocky year — repeated report-builder formatting bugs ("the third report builder problem since May"), stale dashboard data, and a four-day silent ERP sync failure that triggered a demand to escalate "to someone senior, not the queue" — resolves into a run of calm, routine tickets from mid-2025 onward. The customer explicitly confirmed the connector fix ("the fix has held for two weeks now... appreciate someone actually walking us through what changed"), and nothing has reopened since. This is the anger-then-genuine-resolution arc: engaged and vocal, not leaving.
Single onboarding-style ticket about chart types, resolved in two days. No signal either way beyond normal early-stage engagement.

Five spaced-out, routine technical questions (API tokens, connector setup, pagination, conditional formatting, filter defaults) over seven months, all resolved within a week. Healthy, low-drama account.

Extremely high-touch account with repeated same-week bug clusters, always during business-critical periods ("we are literally in close week", "first working day of the year"), and fixes that sometimes don't hold on the first try (API failure recurring the next morning, a seat invite bouncing twice). One ticket explicitly asked for "someone senior on this thread." Despite the volume and visible stress, every issue gets fixed within 1–2 days and the customer says so repeatedly ("appreciate the quick turnarounds, still, five in a week is a lot") — a demanding, engaged account rather than a flight risk, but a support-cost sink where the recurring month-end API instability deserves a root-cause look.

A dashboard-loading fault reported in November 2024 dragged on for over four months despite repeated follow-ups, provoking a formal escalation ("get someone from engineering on this, not tier one support") and, while that was still pending, a second failure that led the customer to write "we are close to reviewing whether this platform is still fit for our team." The fault was then genuinely fixed — confirmed stable for three weeks in a July 2025 ticket, followed by calm, positive traffic through October 2025 ("things have been noticeably smoother since the summer fix"). A real recovery from a near-churn point, not a suppressed problem.

Seven spaced-out tickets over 15 months — export/dashboard bugs and feature questions — each resolved within a week and a half at most. No complaint tone, no recurrence of any issue. Healthy, low-maintenance account.

Seven tickets over seven months, dominated by feature requests (webhooks, incremental sync, report version history) rather than complaints, with explicitly positive notes ("loving the new grouping options", "appreciated the response on the sync question"). An engaged, expanding account building more on the platform.

Sparse but concerning: an ERP connector timeout first reported in December 2024 as "not urgent" recurred in May 2025 with the customer noting it is "slightly more frequent now" and asking if the pattern is "worth a deeper look" — calm language describing a real, worsening fault that was closed as resolved both times with no confirmed root cause. Everything else (export naming, dashboard load time) is routine. Low ticket volume plus a recurring, worsening fault described politely is exactly the quiet pattern worth flagging before it becomes a workaround the customer stops mentioning.

Four widely spaced, routine tickets (rounding question, export scheduling confirmation, format request, new-hire API access) over a year, all resolved without complaint. Healthy, unremarkable account.

competitor_mentions.quote: Dashlume has quoted a bundled per-seat rate
One of our analysts came from a Dashlume shop and asked about pivot-style reports in report builder

narrative: Mostly routine tickets (mobile drill-down, alert timezone, saved filter defaults), but the account is actively benchmarking: in June 2024 they asked for "our current seat breakdown so we can compare properly" against a Dashlume quote, and in March 2025 an analyst "came from a Dashlume shop" and asked about feature parity. Both mentions are matter-of-fact rather than threatening, and 15 months of continued routine engagement since the pricing comparison suggests it didn't move them — but a genuine per-seat price comparison against a named competitor is worth a proactive check-in regardless.

Eight routine tickets over ten months — alert config questions, a UI-move heads-up ("not a bug, just a heads up"), dashboard/report questions — with mildly increasing resolution times through mid-2025 before dropping back down. No anger, no recurrence, no competitor signal. Steady, unremarkable account.

Three tickets over five months tracking a subsidiary integration, entirely positive ("setup was smooth") with sensible feature requests (mapping templates, consolidated exports) as the integration matures. Engaged, expanding account.

Four routine tickets over ten months, ending with a proactive seat audit ahead of renewal ("ahead of our renewal, could you send a current breakdown... so we can true up numbers") — housekeeping, not a red flag. Healthy account showing normal renewal-prep behaviour.

The roughest account in the batch: over 14 months, five distinct threads stacked up simultaneously (seat reassignment, report-builder formulas, dashboards, a connector, exports), with the customer explicitly losing track ("we currently have four separate problems logged against our account") and eventually asking for the account manager directly and "someone senior, not tier one." A call evidently happened, after which the customer confirmed in writing that dashboards, the export bug, and seat reassignment were genuinely fixed ("unlike last year, the change has actually held", "thank you for finally tracing the root cause"). Two threads — the report-builder formula bug from October 2024 and the July 2025 API failures — were never explicitly confirmed fixed and simply stop appearing in the record, so treat them as open until confirmed. The turnaround looks real but this account has been closer to leaving than any other in this batch and needs a check that nothing was quietly dropped.
